sections.h2: How do I reach the Muskegon County register of deeds?
sections.html:
Suite A102 at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Muskegon, MI 49442, is where Muskegon County deeds are filed, and 231-724-6271 reaches the staff. Business hours run 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. on weekdays. Anything to be recorded must arrive by 4:30 p.m. The county calls itself the official recorder and depository of land documents since 1859, the year it was organized out of Ottawa County.

The shelves hold mortgages, liens, surveys, plats, land contracts, condominium filings and financing statements as well as deeds. Transfer tax for both the state and the county is collected at this counter when the deed goes on record.

Writing or advising on a deed is off limits, since MCL 600.916(1) bars clerks from legal advice. The county points owners to title companies, real estate lawyers or off-the-shelf forms that satisfy the state's recording standards.

sections.h2: Can I file by mail, in person or online in Muskegon County?
sections.html:
Counter, mail and online all work, provided the paper has original signatures. Photocopies and faxes come back unrecorded.

Electronic filing goes through CSC, EPN, Indecomm or Simplifile. Some document types stay on paper.

  • Master deeds, and amendments that change a legal description and bring large drawings.
  • Plats.
  • Property transfer affidavits, which go to the equalization department instead.

Your title company can tell you whether it files through one of these vendors.

The office adds two free protections. Home Security Search lets an owner look up records under their own name, and Fraud Guard emails you when your name shows up on a document headed for recording in the county. Both suit a landlord or an owner who holds property for years.

sections.h2: What does the register charge, line by line?
sections.html:
The county's schedule took effect October 1, 2016. Of the $30 recording charge, $4 supports the state survey and remonumentation program. A warranty deed, land contract or other deed with a covenant of warranty also needs a treasurer's tax certificate.

Muskegon County register of deeds charges (source: the county Schedule of Fees page)
ItemCharge
One deed, mortgage or other instrument$30
Each further instrument assigned or discharged in the same document$3
Treasurer's tax certificate$5
Copy of a land record$1 a page
Copy of a recorded plat$2
Certification$5 a document
Minimum search charge$5

Paying by check with a certificate takes two checks: one to the register of deeds covering recording and transfer tax, and one for $5 to the Muskegon County Treasurer.

sections.h2: What does a Muskegon County seller owe in transfer tax?
sections.html:
Selling triggers two taxes on the grantor: $3.75 to the state and $0.55 to the county for each $500 block of price, partial blocks counted whole. At the county's $198,300 median home value that is 397 blocks, which produces $1,488.75 for the state, $218.35 for the county and $1,707.10 in all.

Troubled sales get special treatment, and the county FAQ spells it out. A sheriff's deed always escapes the state tax and only sometimes escapes the county tax. The state act also exempts deeds given in foreclosure or in place of it, and both acts exempt a corrective deed and a spousal conveyance that makes or ends a tenancy by the entirety. Whatever exemption applies, put the wording on the face of the deed.

sections.h2: Which pre-closing steps matter for a Muskegon County seller?
sections.html:
Start with the treasurer's stamp, which shows the parcel's taxes are current. A warranty deed cannot be recorded without it, so any unpaid balance is settled by closing.

The loan is next. A payoff leads the lender to record a discharge, and no new deed is issued. Copies of the discharge or of your deed can be bought at the counter or through the online record search.

  • Pull the current deed so the legal description is copied word for word.
  • List every owner by exact name, since a missing owner means a missing signature.
  • Record a certified death certificate or proof of death if the deed names a survivor.
  • Get the clerk's certification and seal on any court order.

Removing or adding a name takes a new, notarized deed, not an amendment. Recording a certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a fresh deed. A title company or attorney should prepare the paper.

sections.h2: What does the Muskegon County map look like?
sections.html:
Water outweighs land in Muskegon County: 961 of 1,460 square miles are lake, which leaves 499 square miles of ground. Muskegon Lake, fed by the Muskegon River, is Michigan's only deep water port on Lake Michigan, and White Lake and Mona Lake add more shoreline. The river's name comes from an Ojibwa word for marsh. The urban southwest corner holds Muskegon, Muskegon Heights, Roosevelt Park and Norton Shores.

The 2020 census found 175,824 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 177,901. Owners live in 78.1% of housing units. Median home value stands at $198,300 against median rent of $1,028, and the mean trip to work takes 21.6 minutes. Builders took out 451 permits in 2025.

Property forms live with the county equalization department. A new owner sends the transfer affidavit to the city or township assessor, and the principal residence exemption lifts up to 18 mills of school operating tax. Poverty and disabled veteran relief are requested at the local assessor. The county assesses for some of its cities and townships, and the rest do their own.

sections.h2: How do Muskegon, Norton Shores and the lakeshore affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Muskegon city, the county seat, had 38,318 residents in 2020 and wraps around a harbor on Lake Michigan, 42 miles northwest of Grand Rapids. Winters bring heavy lake-effect snow, which is why buyers of older houses ask about roofs and porches. Some neighborhoods began as separate villages: Bluffton, a lumbering village from 1862, was annexed by Muskegon in 1889.

Norton Shores, with 25,030 residents, sits south of the city between Lake Michigan and Mona Lake, and it holds forested dunes in Hoffmaster State Park. Norton Township was split from Ottawa County in 1859, Roosevelt Park began as a 1926 subdivision and became a city in 1946, and Norton Shores incorporated in 1968. Mona Shores Public Schools serves that area. Muskegon Public Schools dates to 1860, and Muskegon Community College hosts programs from several universities.

Downtown Muskegon stretches nearly two miles along the south shore of Muskegon Lake. A convention center opened there in 2021, the Saturday farmers market draws more than 10,000 visitors in summer, and the lumber barons' Hackley and Hume mansions form a historic district. Michigan's Adventure amusement park lies a few miles north of the city.

Beaches, bike trails along Muskegon Lake and a Lake Express ferry to Milwaukee shape how buyers value a lakeside address, and Pere Marquette Beach is the largest free public beach on Lake Michigan's eastern shore. A cottage-style house near Pere Marquette Beach or Mona Lake often draws different offers than a mid-century house inland, and a seller should pin down the parcel's legal description and township before listing.

faqs.q: What is the last time of day a deed can be recorded in Muskegon County?
faqs.a: 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The office itself stays open to 5 p.m., at 1903 Marquette Avenue, Suite A102.

faqs.q: Can a scanned or photocopied deed go on record?
faqs.a: No. Only papers with original signatures are accepted, and a court order must carry the court clerk's certification and seal.

faqs.q: Why might I need two checks at the register of deeds?
faqs.a: The treasurer's $5 certificate for a warranty deed is paid to the Muskegon County Treasurer, separately from the $30 recording fee and any transfer tax.

faqs.q: What would the seller owe in transfer tax on a $198,300 sale?
faqs.a: The total is $1,707.10: $1,488.75 to the state and $218.35 to the county. Any exemption has to be stated on the deed.

faqs.q: How does a co-owner come off a deed?
faqs.a: By a new, notarized deed that is then recorded. Staff cannot draft it, so use a title company or attorney. A certified death certificate takes a deceased owner off title without a new deed.
